newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer due to crude, Europe naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer due to crude, Europe naphtha.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha rebounded in subdued afternoon trade on Monday, taking its direction from overseas crudes as well as northwest European naphtha markets, traders said.
"Firmer crudes and European naphtha gave support to the naphtha market, although regional fundamentals were not so strong," one dealer said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half December was quoted at $207.00/$209.00, compared with late Friday's $205.75/$206.25.
Second-half November was assessed almost at the same level as first-half December cargoes.
In physical naphtha, a petrochemical firm said it bought a second-half November cargo to be delivered to Chiba at slightly above the mean of Japanese quotes late last week.
Prior to the deal, another petrochemical end-user in Chiba, near Tokyo, bought a mid-November cargo at the mean of Japanese quotes minus 50 cents, traders said.

Of 3.8 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for October lifting, Pertamina allocated 300,000 barrels to Pacific Petroleum Trading, 540,000 barrels to Far East Investment and 186,000 barrels to Itochu Corp, traders said. -- Tokyo Commodities (81-3 3432 8837)
